content.title: Orlando Magic Lose Heartbreaker to L.A. Lakers on Last-Second 3-Pointer | Orlando Magic
content.text: March 21, 202610:22 PM EDTORLANDO - Now three of the last four meetings between the Orlando Magic and Los Angeles Lakers have been decided by a go-ahead shot in the final seconds.Last season, Franz Wagner hit a game-winning step-back 3-pointer in L.A. Earlier this year, also in L.A., Wendell Carter Jr. made a go-ahead layup with 6.7 seconds remaining. On Saturday, in Orlando, it was the Lakers that left town with a winning bucket. After a wild sequence of events, which included a lengthy review to determine who touched the ball last on an out-of-bounds play, Luke Kennard drilled the game-winning 3-pointer with 0.6 seconds left to lift L.A. to a 105-104 victory. “They did a helluva job sprinting to the basket. They took two with them,” Magic head coach Jamahl Mosley said. “We didn’t bounce back out fast enough to get to Kennard. And he was able to step back and knock down a three. The communication was stay connected, physical reroutes without fouling and get them inside the line.”The Magic seemed to have control with about a minute left after going up by five following a pair of Paolo Banchero free throws. But an Austin Reaves layup, a Deandre Ayton offensive rebound that led to him getting fouled (made the first free throw and intentionally missed the second), a heads-up defensive play by LeBron James in which he got Banchero to touch the ball last before it went out of bounds, and then Kennard’s winning three propelled L.A. to its ninth straight win.“We have to be better from the beginning part of the game. Can’t have lulls,” Mosley said. “It came down to those last three or four plays essentially. But prior to that, we gave up offensive rebounds. Small things within the game costed us down the stretch. But we just have to be better. Our communication down the stretch (has to be better). You have to give the Lakers a ton of credit there for continuing to battle back and fight and give themselves an opportunity.”Luka Doncic finished with 33 points. It was his ninth straight 30-plus point performance and 40th of the season. Reaves had 26 points and James scored 12. Nobody on the Magic ever got into much of a rhythm. As a team, they shot 42.9 percent from the field and 28.9 percent from 3-point range. Banchero went 4-of-14 from the field and finished with a team-high 16 points, Jalen Suggs had 14, Carter finished with 13 and Desmond Bane and Tristan da Silva each scored 12. Turnovers were a big issue for the Magic, who had 18 of them for 22 Lakers points. L.A. also outscored Orlando 52-36 in the paint and had eight more fast break points. There were 10 lead changes throughout the game. L.A.’s biggest advantage was 14 and Orlando’s was seven. The Magic have now lost four consecutive games after previously winning seven straight. The 19,597 that were in attendance at Saturday's game was the second largest crowd in Magic history. The record is 19,598, set on March 24, 2025, also against the Lakers.They will look to bounce back on Monday when they host the Indiana Pacers at 7 p.m. Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 1:37Remaining Time 1:37Game Highlights: Magic vs. LakersTags(FERNANDO MEDINA)Orlando Magic, Magic Player Jevon Carter and AdventHealth Unveil Refurbished Basketball Court at Oak Ridge High SchoolMarch 25, 20267:12 PM EDTThis marks the seventh basketball court in the local community the Magic and AdventHealth have refurbishedORLANDO – For just about any true basketball enthusiast, there’s a story of a hoop that made them fall in love with the game.Whether it was a driveway setup, school gymnasium, park court, YMCA or a basket on the back of a bedroom door, there’s usually a hoop that helped cultivate their passion for the game.Orlando Magic guard Jevon Carter, who signed with the team as a free agent on Feb. 6, has experienced this firsthand. And that’s why Carter made sure he was in attendance for the unveiling of a collaborative project by the Magic and AdventHealth that aims to bring even more of those stories to life.On Wednesday, as part of the Magic and AdventHealth's continuing commitment to the local community, the two teamed up to unveil a newly refurbished basketball court at Oak Ridge High School.Carter along with Magic Executive Vice President of Marketing and Social Responsibility Shelly Wilkes, AdventHealth East Orlando Chief Operating Officer Paul Adeogun, members of the Magic staff and community leaders were on hand to celebrate the occasion with a basketball clinic for students from Oak Ridge High School.The Magic provided lunch, team basketballs and other gifts for the over 30 youth in attendance.The court was a collaborative effort between the Magic, AdventHealth, and Oak Ridge High School. The Magic and AdventHealth also teamed up with artist Swish Dreams, ACE Courts, and GAF to provide sustainable and heat-resistant paint for longevity of the court.“It’s dope,” said Carter. “(The Magic) and AdventHealth do a great job of refurbishing a court every year. They did a fantastic job. Even the artist that painted the court did an amazing job. It’s good to come out, spend time with the kids and give them hope to keep striving and keep going for your dreams.”Carter recently contributed to the refurbishment of his childhood court, 10th park back in Maywood, Illinois. It helped his passion for basketball blossom and now bears a tribute to him along with other contributors and professional athletes that grew up in the area.For the Magic and AdventHealth, this is the seventh of 20 courts that they plan to refurbish in the Central Florida area. The courts completed include Wicklow Elementary (August 2021), the Callahan Center (May 2022), the James R. Smith Neighborhood Center (March 2023), Lee P. Moore Park (on April 5), Kissimmee City Chamber Park Community Center (Jan. 2024), Coastline Park in Sanford (March 2025) and the current one – Oak Ridge High School (March 2026).“This is our seventh court that we’ve done with AdventHealth and the commitment is 20,” Wilkes explained. “We hope to actually do even more than that over time. Really the goal of this is a commitment to the community that really is truly at the foundation of who the Orlando Magic are and of who AdventHealth is. Hopefully this not only inspires the next generation of basketball fans, but also keeps kids active.”As an original Champions of the Community partners, AdventHealth has been working with the Magic on community projects that impact and benefit Central Florida. Magic Champions of the Community partners represent organizations that are committed to improving the lives of all Central Floridians. Since the Magic and AdventHealth partnership began back in 1989, they continue to grow their approach in community programming, unparalleled branding and category exclusivity in the area of healthcare while expanding their commitment to the local community.“It’s so exciting to see AdventHealth and the Magic be a part of making sure (children) have a safe place to play,” Adeogun said. “A safe place to make sure that everyone is healthy, (even in terms of) mental health. We have a campaign with the Orlando Magic – the ‘You Good’ campaign – to make sure kids are doing well. We’re supporting them as best that we can, so our community can continue to grow.”TagsDespite Strong Offensive Night, Orlando Magic Unable to Slow Down Cleveland CavaliersMarch 25, 202612:07 AM EDTCLEVELAND - When you don’t have, arguably, your four best defenders, it’s going to be tough to play to your standard on that end.That’s precisely what we’ve seen with the Orlando Magic these last couple games. Again playing without Franz Wagner, Jalen Suggs, Anthony Black and Jonathan Isaac, the Magic were unable to slow down the Cleveland Cavaliers in Tuesday’s 136-131 defeat at Rocket Arena.Although the Magic hung tough throughout and were within striking distance down the stretch, their inability to keep the Cavs out of the paint or get out to shooters on the perimeter fast enough was too much to overcome.The Cavs, who outscored the Magic 62-38 in the paint, shot 60 percent from the field overall and 40 percent from 3-point range. It was just the second time this season a Magic opponent reached both those marks in the same game. Cleveland’s efficiency wasn’t just about what Orlando wasn’t able to do defensively, however. The Cavs, pure and simple, have two incredible shot-makers in Donovan Mitchell and James Harden.Mitchell, the league’s seventh-leading scorer, erupted for 42 points and made the game-sealing floater with 13.7 seconds left. Harden, acquired around the trade deadline from the Clippers, tallied 26 points. “Those are two of the best one-on-one scorers in the league,” Paolo Banchero said. “Harden kind of started it off and then Mitchell got it going as the game went on. He’s always a tough cover for us. It seemed like every time we got within a one-possession, two-possession game, they made a shot or got a three for somebody else. You have to just tip your cap to players like that.”Evan Mobley had a solid all-around night with 19 points, nine rebounds and six assists, as did Sam Merrill, who also scored 19. Offense was not an issue at all for Orlando, which shot 49 percent overall, 36 percent from beyond the arc and 92 percent from the free throw line. Banchero posted 36 points on 10-of-19 floor shooting, 3-of-7 3-point shooting and 13-of-15 free throw shooting. It was his 12th 30-plus-point performance of the season. Tristan da Silva registered 18 points, Desmond Bane chipped in with 17 points and Jamal Cain, making his first start of the season and second of his NBA career, also scored 17, a season high for him. “I was comfortable for sure,” Cain said. “My trainer and I have been training for these moments for a reason.I think I’ve been playing okay. I feel like I can play better – a lot better. Ultimately, I’ve been playing confident, just trying to play hard. Just trying to bring juice to the team, bring extra effort and bring anything I can to contribute to winning.”The Magic have now lost six consecutive games after previously winning seven straight.There was a piece of good news on the injury front. Franz, who has missed 43 of Orlando’s last 47 games with his left ankle injury, practiced with the Osceola Magic, the organization’s G League team, on Monday. Although there’s still no timetable for his return, this is encouraging as he continues with his treatment. Orlando will look to snap its losing streak on Thursday when the Sacramento Kings come to Kia Center.
